title: Pars plana vitrectomy for retinal detachment
subtitle: Small-gauge ports, vitrectomy, retinal reattachment, laser and tamponade

sources.title: Posterior Vitreous Detachment, Retinal Breaks, and Lattice Degeneration Preferred Practice Pattern
Scleral buckling versus primary vitrectomy in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment: a prospective randomized multicenter clinical study

indications: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (particularly pseudophakic, with posterior breaks, or vitreous haemorrhage).
Non-clearing vitreous haemorrhage, macular hole, epiretinal membrane, endophthalmitis and other indications per specialist practice.
contraindications: Operator or unit without vitreoretinal expertise: this is a specialist operation, included here for awareness and for the trainee who assists.
preparation: Document macula on or off, the breaks and extent; plan tamponade.

Consent: failure and re-detachment, cataract, raised pressure, the gas bubble and the need to posture, no flying or nitrous oxide anaesthesia while gas remains, endophthalmitis, and silicone oil removal later if used.
positioning: Supine with the head flat and level, chin and forehead in one horizontal plane, a head ring or gel pillow; the head of the patient at the end of the table so the surgeon can sit.
equipment: Vitrectomy machine with cutter, light pipe and wide-angle viewing system, 23G, 25G or 27G trocar cannulas, infusion line, endolaser, perfluorocarbon liquid, gases (SF6, C3F8) or silicone oil, scleral depressor.
anatomy: The pars plana (3.5 to 4 mm behind the limbus), the vitreous base and its attachment to the peripheral retina, the retinal breaks, the macula and optic disc.
criticalSafety: Confirm the infusion cannula tip is inside the vitreous cavity before turning the infusion on.
Give the patient a gas warning wristband and posture instructions.
commonErrors: Iatrogenic retinal breaks at the vitreous base.
Expansile gas concentration causing a pressure spike.
complications: Gas expansion with flying or nitrous oxide.
postop: Posturing as instructed; gas wristband on; no flying or high altitude until the gas has gone.
Steroid, antibiotic and pressure drops as needed; review the next day.
Same-day return for pain, falling vision or a shadow.

steps.emphasis: Mark the eye; record macula on or off, which sets the urgency.
Confirm the eye, the tamponade agent and its concentration; tell the anaesthetist not to use nitrous oxide.
Supine with the head flat and level, chin and forehead in one horizontal plane, a head ring or gel pillow; the head of the patient at the end of the table so the surgeon can sit.
Remove the cannulas and check each sclerotomy for a leak; suture any that leak, especially with gas or oil.
Gas wristband on, posture explained in writing, no flying or nitrous oxide.

step.ppv.ports.title: Placing the trocar cannulas and the infusion
step.ppv.ports.why: The infusion maintains the eye's pressure throughout. If its tip lies under the choroid or retina when it is turned on, fluid floods the suprachoroidal or subretinal space.
how: Insert three trocar cannulas through the pars plana 3.5 mm (pseudophakic) or 4 mm (phakic) behind the limbus, with an oblique tunnel.
Connect the infusion to the inferotemporal cannula.
Look through the pupil and confirm the cannula tip is in the vitreous cavity before turning the infusion on.
pitfalls: Turning on the infusion before seeing the tip.
Placing cannulas too anterior in a phakic eye.

step.ppv.core.title: Core vitrectomy and posterior vitreous detachment
step.ppv.core.why: Removing the vitreous relieves traction on the retina. The vitreous base, where it is firmly attached, is shaved carefully to avoid new breaks.
how: Remove the central vitreous with a high cut rate and moderate vacuum under wide-angle viewing.
Induce a posterior vitreous detachment if not present (triamcinolone helps visualise the gel).
Shave the vitreous base with scleral depression, especially around the breaks.

step.ppv.retina.title: Flattening the retina and treating the breaks
step.ppv.retina.why: The retina must be flat and every break sealed with laser or cryotherapy, or it will detach again.
how: Drain subretinal fluid through a break or a drainage retinotomy, or flatten with perfluorocarbon liquid.
Apply endolaser around every break (and 360 degrees if planned).

step.ppv.tamponade.title: Fluid-air exchange and tamponade
step.ppv.tamponade.why: The gas or oil holds the retina against the wall while the laser scars mature. The wrong gas concentration can raise the pressure dangerously.
how: Exchange fluid for air, draining residual subretinal fluid.
Inject the tamponade: a non-expansile gas mixture (for example SF6 about 20%, C3F8 about 14%) or silicone oil.
